clue.text: Covered in mud thus, I played initially

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
taken as written
in card games, to lead is to play the first card of a trick

explanation.surface: A footballer explains the muddy kit: that is how it looked after the opening of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but 'played initially' is one idea: the card player who goes first leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtied or stained clothing is soiled, and mud is the commonest dirt on a sports pitch.

clue.text: Some collaborator I organised for work done in church

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the letters of the following words is used

parts.note: inside collab_..._rganised

explanation.surface: A partner arranged a service of worship in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A large musical composition for choir and orchestra on a sacred theme, often performed in churches.

clue.text: Computer operators view real broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Computer users are watching a real-life television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast suggests television, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon for the people who use computers, as opposed to hardware and software.

clue.text: Rogue found briefly desirable by a party

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its ending

parts.note: desperate, in the sense of keenly wanted or badly needed, standing in for desirable
A plus DO, a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A villain turns out to be attractive to the guests at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The equation of desirable with desperate is loose; the grid letters confirm the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw or bandit is a rogue, especially one in the Wild West.

clue.text: Computer's essential, therefore, with newspaper articles

parts.note: so can mean therefore
the Financial Times, a British daily
ware means manufactured articles, goods for sale

explanation.surface: A tech writer argues that newspaper features are an essential part of computing.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the standard abbreviation for the Financial Times, a London business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Without programs a machine does nothing, so the programs are a necessary component of any working computer.

clue.text: Provide with requirement, according to this law

parts.note: to supply is to provide
with means along with, and
a demand is a requirement

explanation.surface: A legal instruction to provide something together with a stated requirement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes last and points back at the whole: the clue's own wordplay describes the economic law.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic principle that prices settle where the quantity offered meets the quantity wanted.

clue.text: The brake is needed in that situation

parts.note: taken as written
a rein is a check or restraint, as in to rein in

explanation.surface: A driving instructor explains that the brake is required at that point.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means in that place or in that matter, as in legal language.

clue.text: Outside US city, put up painting

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means written upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Los Angeles
a fresco is a painting on wet plaster

explanation.surface: Outside an American city someone hangs a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside looks like a container signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase describes doing something in the open air, such as eating outdoors.

clue.text: Parts of listener's equipment are damaged by loud instruments

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so the short word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of are, rearranged
drums are noisy percussion instruments

explanation.surface: A hi-fi enthusiast complains that the speakers have been wrecked by loud drumming.
explanation.walkthrough: Equipment suggests stereo gear, but the listener's equipment is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The membranes inside the ear vibrate with sound and are part of the body's hearing apparatus.

clue.text: Partitions Turkey, for example?

parts.note: surface reading: dividing up the country of Turkey
setter's reading: a turkey is the classic bird one slices at the dinner table, and dividing a territory uses the same phrase

explanation.surface: A historian describes the division of the Ottoman state after a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T disguises the roast bird as the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to slice meat for serving and to divide territory between rival powers.

clue.text: One who succeeds, finding iron in Jersey at early stage

indicators.note: the successor is found holding the metal, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an heir succeeds to a title or estate
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A detective finds an iron in a jersey belonging to someone who has just inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is not a sweater but a breed of dairy cow, from the Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow that has not yet calved is the youthful stage of any dairy breed, Jerseys included.

clue.text: With jam left out, roll that's gripped by teeth

indicators.note: left out tells us the letter standing for left is omitted from the word

parts.note: to clog is to jam or block
L is the usual abbreviation for left
to wheel is to roll along

explanation.surface: A child complains that the jam has been left out of a sandwich roll and the bread sticks to the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel meshes with the teeth of another wheel, so it is held and driven by teeth.

clue.text: Encountered extraterrestrial leader or traveller in space

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recounts meeting the head of an alien race, or perhaps some other space voyager.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a rock hurtling through the heavens, a natural voyager among the planets.

clue.text: Call up again, keen to be involved with a war

indicators.note: being involved suggests getting tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reservist is recalled to the army and is eager to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' suggests military conscription, but the definition means rousing from sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone from sleep a second time, or revive a memory, is to summon it back into consciousness.

clue.text: Exuberant English bulletin half-changed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: half-changed means only part of the word is altered in order while the rest stays

parts.note: the first half, BULL, stays; the second half, ETIN, is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful English news broadcast has been partly rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Overflowing with enthusiasm and high spirits, full of energy, the adjective describes lively cheerfulness.

clue.text: Pro's spoken warning to golfers

indicators.note: spoken means we go by how the word is said rather than how it is written

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A golf professional shouts a warning down the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: Pro looks like a golf professional, but it is the Latin word meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers shout this word to alert people ahead who might be hit by a stray ball.

clue.text: Understood rich daughter retaining place to live

indicators.note: retaining means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fat can mean rich, as in a fat profit
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a home is a place to live

explanation.surface: Someone grasped why a wealthy daughter kept the family house.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the daughter does the retaining; the rich part simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of a mystery is to comprehend it, as a sounding line measures depth.

clue.text: Smarten, somehow, with new bits of clothing

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters fall into an order we must work out

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone advises tidying up an outfit with a few new garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover pieces of fabric from a bolt of cloth are sold as offcuts, the sense meant here.

clue.text: Charged particles irradiated our nuclear submarines initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A news story about radioactive particles contaminating the navy's atomic submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms that have gained or lost electrons carry an electric charge and are the particles meant.

clue.text: Highly placed within churches, provides encouragement

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: up in the tall pointed towers of churches
second meaning: stimulates or motivates someone

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's position in the church gives heart to others.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is whimsical: split the answer into two words to find where something lofty in a church sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with the urge or ability to act is to motivate them; split, the word locates something in church towers.

clue.text: Someone other than me on a lake? That's ideal

parts.note: not I is someone other than me
taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone pictures another person out on a lake and thinks it perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Ideal looks like praise for the lake scene, but it means existing only as an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypothetical or existing only in theory, a sense of the adjective shared with imaginary rather than real.

clue.text: Kindly act that should be applauded

definitions.text: Kindly act that should be applauded

parts.note: setter's reading: a favour done for someone
surface reading: a fine performance on stage that earns clapping

explanation.walkthrough: A turn is also a variety performer's act, so a good one deserves applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpful deed done for someone is a favour, and a music-hall act is also called a turn.

clue.text: Means of transmission of financial ratio

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the set of gears that passes power along in a machine
second meaning: a company's debt measured against its equity

explanation.surface: A question about how money is transferred within a financial system.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the toothed wheels in a drivetrain and, in British finance, a firm's borrowing compared to shareholders' capital.

clue.text: Ketch reportedly put in building for certain craft

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the words said aloud rather than read them

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious English executioner, whose work was to hang people

explanation.surface: A sailing boat is stored inside a boathouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, but here it is Jack Ketch, the 17th-century hangman, whose order would be 'hang her'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are kept and serviced in a large shed, and aeroplanes are the craft intended.

clue.text: Part of sentence cut, that's understood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an omission of words from a sentence
second meaning: the dropped words are ones the reader supplies from context

explanation.surface: A prisoner's term has been reduced, and everyone accepts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sentence suggests a prison term, but it is the grammatical unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the omission of words whose meaning the reader supplies from context.

clue.text: Standing stone pieces in this place, reportedly

parts.note: chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Someone describes fragments of rock lying around this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces suggests fragments of the stone, but it means chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric upright monolith, like those in Brittany, is known by this Breton name.

clue.text: With Jack., Queen, King, and Ace no trump is not normal

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
Elizabeth Regina
R for Rex, Latin for king
A is the ace in a pack of cards
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bridge player holding all the honour cards finds a no-trump bid strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture hides that jack means a sailor. The definition carries 'is' along with 'not normal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deviating from the usual course or standard is abnormal, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Meant to include evidence in legal document

indicators.note: to include means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
a sign is evidence or an indication

explanation.surface: A lawyer intended to put proof into a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: If something was done on purpose it was intended, planned with that purpose in mind.

clue.text: You and the French surrounding ship in struggle

indicators.note: surrounding means the French words go around the vessel's abbreviation

parts.note: tu is French for you
le is French for the
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An English sailor and some French crew have a fight on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' does double duty: it also tells you to put 'You' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous scuffle or close fight is a struggle, a synonym used as a noun.
